methodological_rigor.justification: This is a pre-specified pooled analysis of CCA patients from two independent, single-arm, open-label phase II/IIa studies (RAGNAR NCT04083976 and LUC2001 NCT02699606). The primary endpoint (ORR) was BIRC-assessed using RECIST v1.1, which reduces assessment bias, and both source studies had similar dosing. Key weaknesses: single-arm pooled design without control arm; heterogeneity between RAGNAR (global, 15 countries, 21-day cycles, CTCAE v5.0) and LUC2001 (Asia-only, 28-day cycles, CTCAE v4.0); tumor assessment intervals differ (6 vs 8 weeks); anatomic CCA subtype data not collected; small LUC2001 contribution (n=12). Statistics are appropriate (Clopper-Pearson, Kaplan-Meier) but no sensitivity analysis addressing between-study heterogeneity; the cross-trial comparison with pemigatinib/futibatinib in the discussion is acknowledged as non-definitive.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a pooled analysis of individual single-arm cohort-like trials, mapping to Oxford LoE 2b. Clinical relevance is substantial: CCA is a disease with few post-first-line options, and the observed 55.1% ORR (95% CI 43.4-66.4) and 18.1-month median OS in a pretreated FGFR-altered population are meaningful and numerically competitive with approved FGFR inhibitors pemigatinib and futibatinib. The inclusion of responders with FGFR2 mutations and FGFR3 fusions extends the actionable biomarker set and could inform precision oncology practice.

reporting_quality.justification: As a pooled analysis of two single-arm phase II trials, no single reporting standard applies perfectly; elements of CONSORT (for the parent trials, referenced) and STROBE are relevant. Methods adequately describe eligibility, dosing (including 8 to 9 mg up-titration), BIRC tumor assessment, MedDRA coding, and CTCAE grading differences between studies. Patient flow (78 patients, RAGNAR n=66, LUC2001 n=12) and key demographics are clearly reported. Data availability is not explicitly stated in the provided text; the parent trial registrations are cited, but a data-sharing statement, protocol/SAP, and code availability are not visible.

novelty_literature.justification: The work provides the first pooled, disease-specific analysis of erdafitinib in FGFR-altered CCA combining RAGNAR and LUC2001, and notes that erdafitinib may be the only FGFR inhibitor with confirmed responses in both FGFR2 fusions and FGFR2 mutations and FGFR3 alterations per the authors. This is a meaningful incremental extension in a competitive FGFR inhibitor landscape already dominated by approved agents (pemigatinib, futibatinib). It is not a first-in-class discovery but provides clinically useful consolidation and cross-study signal in a disease with limited second-line options.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with clear IMRaD structure, efficient summary of source trial designs, and a discussion that appropriately contextualizes findings against pemigatinib/futibatinib while acknowledging cross-trial comparison limitations. Tables and figures (including waterfall-type tumor reduction plots and a co-alteration heatmap) communicate the efficacy and safety signals clearly. Numerical reporting includes 95% CIs consistently. Minor issues: a few places have placeholder [REDACTED] text from PubChem/Gene ID annotations that disrupt readability, and genomic-data nomenclature occasionally overloads the prose.

key_strengths: Pre-specified pooled analysis of two registered phase II trials (RAGNAR, LUC2001) with BIRC-assessed ORR as primary endpoint
Largest reported erdafitinib-in-CCA dataset to date (n=78) with diverse racial representation (47.4% White, 38.5% Asian)
Demonstrates responses across FGFR2 fusions, FGFR2 mutations, and FGFR3-TACC3 fusions, expanding the potentially actionable alteration set beyond FGFR2 fusions
Safety profile consistent with known erdafitinib adverse event pattern (hyperphosphatemia 83%, stomatitis 72%) with manageable dose modifications and no treatment-related deaths
key_concerns: Single-arm pooled design without randomized comparator; cross-trial comparisons to pemigatinib/futibatinib are numerical only and confounded by differences in patient selection and follow-up
Study heterogeneity between RAGNAR and LUC2001 (cycle length, imaging interval, CTCAE version) not addressed by sensitivity analysis
Anatomic CCA subtype (intrahepatic vs perihilar vs distal) not captured, limiting subgroup interpretation
Co-alteration analysis limited to RAGNAR (n=66) and underpowered (23 patients with co-alterations); p-value reported without adjustment
No explicit data availability/code sharing statement; parent-trial SAP details not reproduced
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent, clinically useful pooled analysis of a rare molecularly-defined CCA population, strengthened by BIRC-adjudicated endpoints but limited by single-arm pooled design and cross-study heterogeneity; appropriate for Tier 3 oncology journals (e.g., Cancers, European Journal of Cancer, BMC Cancer) with minor revisions.
